value: McCulloch & Pitts publish 'A logical calculus of the ideas immanent in nervous activity' (1943), the first formal model of a neural network.
Dartmouth Summer Research Project on Artificial Intelligence (summer 1956), proposed in a document dated 31 Aug 1955 that introduced the term 'artificial intelligence'.
Epoch's notable set starts with Shannon's Theseus maze mouse (1950, ~40 FLOP); Rosenblatt's Mark I Perceptron (1957) is ~6.95×10^5 FLOP.
Dartmouth workshop (about 18 Jun–17 Aug 1956 per Solomonoff's notes).

DARPA cuts back undirected AI research in 1973–74 (e.g. cancelling ~$3M a year of Speech Understanding Research grants at CMU), following the 1969 Mansfield Amendment and the UK Lighthill report (published early 1973).
Commercial expert systems arrive: McDermott's R1/XCON paper (AAAI 1980) and deployment at Digital Equipment Corporation (in production by about 1980–81).
No compute series point; Epoch's database is sparse for 1974–1980.
R1/XCON at DEC (1980); Japan's Fifth Generation Computer Systems project (ICOT) launched 1982 with a ~¥54 billion ten-year budget.
Collapse of the market for specialised Lisp machines (1987) as general-purpose workstations and PCs became powerful enough to run the same software.
Convention: early-1990s end of the expert-systems retrenchment and of Japan's FGCS project (ten-year term to 1992); statistical and machine-learning methods move centre-stage.
IBM Watson wins Jeopardy! (Feb 2011) and Siri ships (Oct 2011) — the last major milestones before deep learning took over.
AlexNet wins ILSVRC 2012 (results 30 Sep 2012) with 15.3% top-5 error vs 26.2% for the runner-up.
'Attention Is All You Need' (arXiv 12 Jun 2017) introduces the Transformer.
Largest estimated runs rose from ~6×10^17 FLOP (2012) to ~6.6×10^21 FLOP (GNMT, 2016) in Epoch's notable set; AlexNet itself was 4.7×10^17.
Transformer 7.4×10^18 FLOP (2017) → PaLM 2.5×10^24 FLOP (2022): ~340,000× in five years (DERIVED: 2.5e24 / 7.4e18).
ChatGPT (30 Nov 2022); UBS estimated 100M monthly users by January 2023.
OpenAI o1-preview (12 Sep 2024) opens the reasoning-model era; Anthropic's computer use (22 Oct 2024) opens the agent era.
GPT-4 2.1×10^25 FLOP and ~$78M estimated training cost (2023).
Largest estimated training run: GPT-6 Astra ~9.4×10^26 FLOP (Sep 2026, Epoch via secondary source); SWE-bench Verified saturated at ~97% (Sep 2026).
First mathematical model of a network of simplified neurons computing logical functions.
McCulloch & Pitts, Bulletin of Mathematical Biophysics 5

Replaces 'Can machines think?' with the imitation game (Turing test). Turing predicted that in about 50 years machines with ~10^9 storage would leave an average interrogator no more than a 70% chance of a correct identification after five minutes.
McCarthy, Minsky, Rochester and Shannon propose a summer study; the document introduces the term. Proposed as a '2 month, 10 man study'.
AI Magazine reprint of the proposal
Conventional founding event of AI as a field. Ran roughly 18 Jun–17 Aug 1956 (about eight weeks) per Solomonoff's notes; other accounts say six weeks.

First learning machine to attract mass publicity; the US Navy's ONR demonstrated it in July 1958 (a simulation on an IBM 704). Mark I Perceptron used a 400-sensor 'retina' and ~1,000 weights; Epoch estimates its training compute at ~6.95×10^5 FLOP.
Rosenblatt, Psychological Review 65(6) 1958; Wikipedia Mark I Perceptron
First mobile robot to reason about its own actions; its STRIPS planner became the basis for later automated planners.
Weizenbaum's pattern-matching 'therapist' program; first widely known chatbot and first demonstration of people over-attributing understanding to software.
US law pushes DARPA toward mission-oriented research; Minsky & Papert's book highlights single-layer perceptron limits.
UK Science Research Council review concludes AI had failed its grand promises; UK funding is sharply curtailed. Debated on BBC TV in June 1973.
Marks the start of the first AI winter in the US. DARPA cancelled ~$3M a year of Speech Understanding Research grants at Carnegie Mellon.
First commercially significant expert system; starts the expert-systems boom. Most sources put savings at ~$25M a year; by 1986 it had processed 80,000 orders at 95–98% accuracy.
Ten-year MITI programme for logic-programming computers; spurred Western counter-programmes. Initial budget ~¥54 billion over ten years; total spending a little under ¥57 billion (~$320M) by the end.
Rumelhart, Hinton & Williams show multi-layer networks learn useful internal representations. Nature 323:533–536.
End of dedicated AI hardware boom marks the second AI winter; same year NETtalk shows a neural net learning to pronounce text. NETtalk training compute ~2.8×10^10 FLOP (Epoch).

value: First defeat of a reigning world chess champion by a computer in a match under tournament conditions. Won the rematch 3½–2½ (two wins, one loss, three draws); evaluated ~200 million positions per second. Kasparov had won the 1996 match 4–2.
Hochreiter & Schmidhuber's long short-term memory, the recurrent architecture behind most sequence models until the Transformer.
LeCun et al.'s convolutional network for handwriting recognition, deployed for cheque reading. Training compute ~2.8×10^12 FLOP (Epoch, 'Confident').
Stanford's Stanley completes a 132-mile desert course autonomously, a year after no vehicle finished. 6 h 53 min 58 s; in 2004 the best vehicle managed ~7.4 miles.
Hinton, Osindero & Teh show deep networks can be trained layer by layer, reviving neural-network research.
Establishes the benchmark that later showcased deep learning. Winning top-5 error 28.2% (NEC-UIUC).
Open-domain question answering beats the show's two best champions on TV. Two-game totals: Watson $77,147; Ken Jennings $24,000; Brad Rutter $21,600.
First voice assistant in mainstream consumer use.

GPU-trained deep convolutional net wins by a wide margin, triggering the deep-learning era. Top-5 error 15.3% vs 26.2% for the second-best entry; ~60M parameters; trained on two GTX 580 GPUs; ~4.7×10^17 FLOP (Epoch).
Krizhevsky, Sutskever & Hinton, NIPS 2012; Epoch AI
Big Tech begins buying frontier AI labs. Price undisclosed; reported at $400M (Re/code) to more than $500M (The Information).
Goodfellow et al. introduce GANs, the main image-generation method until diffusion models.
Sutskever, Vinyals & Le show end-to-end neural machine translation with LSTMs. Training compute ~5.6×10^19 FLOP (Epoch).
Residual networks win ILSVRC 2015. Top-5 error 3.57%, below the 5.1% single-annotator human estimate.
First defeat of a 9-dan Go professional without handicap, a decade earlier than many expected. 4–1 in Seoul, 9–15 Mar 2016; AlphaGo had beaten Fan Hui 5–0 in Oct 2015 (Nature, 27 Jan 2016).
'Attention Is All You Need' introduces the architecture behind every frontier language model since. 28.4 BLEU on WMT14 English–German; ~7.4×10^18 FLOP training compute (Epoch).

Learns Go from self-play alone, without human games; among the first models trained on >10^23 FLOP. ~6.5×10^20 FLOP of direct training compute (Epoch, 'Confident'); OpenAI's 2018 figure of ~3.4×10^23 included self-play data generation.

value: First widely cited measurement of exploding training compute. More than 300,000× growth from AlexNet to AlphaGo Zero; 3.4-month doubling time (2012–2018).
Pre-trained bidirectional Transformer resets most language-understanding benchmarks. BERT-Large ~340M parameters; ~2.8×10^20 FLOP (Epoch).
OpenAI withholds the full model at first over misuse concerns, starting the release-norms debate. 1.5B parameters; ~1.9×10^21 FLOP (Epoch).
Shows few-shot learning emerges from scale. 175B parameters; 3.14×10^23 FLOP; 43.9% on MMLU (few-shot); ~$4.3M estimated training cost (AI Index 2024).
Effectively solves single-chain protein structure prediction, a 50-year-old problem. Median 92.4 GDT across all targets (≈90 is considered competitive with experiment).
Largest dense model of its time; strong reasoning results. 540B parameters; ~2.5×10^24 FLOP (Epoch).
Stable Diffusion released with open weights
High-quality image generation runs on consumer hardware.
Generative AI becomes a mass consumer product. 1M users in five days (OpenAI); UBS estimated 100M monthly users by January 2023 from Similarweb data.
Capable model weights spread beyond big labs (leaked publicly in early March), seeding the open-weight ecosystem. 7B–65B parameters.

Frontier model with strong exam performance; sets the 'GPT-4 class' bar. 86.4% MMLU; ~2.1×10^25 FLOP and ~$78M training compute cost (Epoch/AI Index); OpenAI's 'top 10% of bar takers' claim was later disputed.
Open letter calls for a six-month pause on training systems more powerful than GPT-4.
First intergovernmental summit on frontier-AI risk; Bletchley Declaration.
OpenAI's first own disclosure of the 100M mark (weekly users). 100M weekly active users at OpenAI's first DevDay.

Google's first frontier multimodal model; most expensive training run estimated at the time. ~5.0×10^25 FLOP (Epoch, 'Speculative'); ~$191M cloud-basis cost in AI Index 2024 (Epoch's current CSV: $206M cloud, $30.7M amortised in 2023 USD).
Open-weight model at near-frontier scale. ~3.8×10^25 FLOP (6 × 405B params × 15.6T tokens); ~$170M estimated cost (AI Index 2025).
EU AI Act enters into force
First comprehensive AI statute in a major economy; obligations phase in from Feb 2025. Maximum fines €35M or 7% of worldwide turnover.

Models trained to 'think' before answering; inference-time compute becomes a scaling axis. OpenAI reported o1 solved 83% of AIME (the US IMO qualifier) problems with 64-sample consensus vs 13% for GPT-4o; o1-preview ~57%.
Physics to Hopfield and Hinton (8 Oct); half of Chemistry to Hassabis and Jumper for AlphaFold (9 Oct).
First frontier model offered with the ability to operate a desktop GUI; start of the agent era.
Large jumps on hard reasoning benchmarks. ARC-AGI-1 75.7% within the $10k limit (87.5% high-compute); FrontierMath 25.2% (OpenAI-run; Epoch's own later run ~10%); SWE-bench Verified 71.7%.
Private US AI-infrastructure commitment marks the gigawatt-scale data-centre era. $500B over four years, $100B immediately.
Chinese open-weight reasoning model near the frontier at far lower prices. Nvidia lost ~$589B of market value on 27 Jan 2025 (Bloomberg; Reuters says ~$593B), a record one-day loss.
Epoch's first estimate of a training run above 10^26 FLOP. ~3.5×10^26 FLOP (Epoch CSV, 'Likely'; ~80,000 H100s for ~3 months).
Natural-language maths at olympiad gold level within contest time. 35/42 (5 of 6 problems), Gemini Deep Think, certified by the IMO.
Largest estimated run of 2025. ~5×10^26 FLOP and ~$490M (Epoch median: 246M H100-hours).

Flagship launched at lower price than predecessors; Epoch estimates it used less training compute than GPT-4.5. ~6.6×10^25 FLOP (Epoch CSV, 'Speculative', CI 2e25–2e26) vs ~3.8×10^26 for GPT-4.5; $1.25 / $10 per million input/output tokens.
Consumer AI reaches roughly a tenth of humanity weekly. 800M weekly active users.
Claude Opus 4.5 passes 80% on SWE-bench Verified
